CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Lawrence is a 62-year-old male with past medical history of Type I diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, and reflux who presents with shortness of breath for approximately 10 days. Patient attributes swelling to attending house parties and consuming salty foods and reports feeling lethargic. Dyspnea occurs with exertion, specifically with walking up stairs, but not at rest while sitting. Patient endorses leg swelling and mild discomfort when lying flat in bed. Reports morning stiffness upon waking that requires time to adjust. Patient reports one episode of acute shortness of breath at night approximately one week ago without recurrence. Regarding Type I diabetes managed with insulin pump, patient reports blood sugars are adequately controlled with good monitoring during work week, though forgets to monitor on weekends; denies recent spikes. Patient acknowledges fondness for chocolate bars. Regarding depression, patient reports difficult year and a half with trial of outdoor morning stretches in summer; now seeking alternatives due to weather changes and not yet ready for medications but open to suggestions. For reflux, patient continues on omeprazole with lifestyle modifications including reduction of Red Bull and caffeine; alcohol intake was challenging during holidays but improving. Patient denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for shortness of breath. Negative for chest pain, fever, chills, cough, or abdominal pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type I diabetes, congestive heart failure, depression, reflux.

MEDICATIONS
Insulin pump, Omeprazole.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Attends house parties. Consumes salty foods. Enjoys chocolate bars. Works during week with busy weekends. Previously performed outdoor stretches in summer. Reducing alcohol and caffeine intake.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs good. Pulse oximetry good. Neck: No jugular venous distension, no carotid bruits. Heart: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated. Lungs: Bilateral basilar crackles appreciated. Lower extremities: 1+ pitting edema appreciated.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No evidence of airspace disease.
Labs: No elevated white blood cell count.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute heart failure exacerbation: Started on Lasix 40 mg daily. Patient instructed to weigh himself daily and contact provider if weight is stable or increasing. Instructed to call or go to emergency room if shortness of breath worsens at rest, as intravenous diuretics may be needed.

2. Type I diabetes: Hemoglobin A1C to be checked in approximately one month to assess need for medication adjustments. Patient to follow up with endocrinologist. Ensure patient has had recent eye exam.

3. Depression: Referral to psychiatry for talk therapy. No medications initiated at this time.

4. Reflux: Continue Omeprazole 20 mg daily.
